Yeah, pretty much (Copy/Pasting a Gemini assisted answer below) The Funda: often mistaken Identity & False Origin of trends🤔 The tenuous connection is that the popular name or perceived origin of each item is, to some degree, incorrect, misleading, or based on a false attribution (often a person or place).  * 🔪 Caesarean Section:    * Misconception: Named after Julius Caesar.    * Reality: The name likely comes from the Latin verb caedere meaning "to cut."  * 🥗 Caesar Salad:    * Misconception: Named after Julius Caesar.    * Reality: Named after restaurateur Caesar Cardini, who invented it in Tijuana, Mexico.  * 🦜 Canary Islands:    * Misconception: Named after the Canary bird.    * Reality: Named after the large dogs (canis) found there by ancient explorers. (The bird was named after the islands.)  * 👒 Panama Hat:    * Misconception: Made in Panama.    * Reality: Woven in Ecuador. It got its name because it was shipped through the Panama Canal.  * 💖 Bae:    * Misconception (Backronym): Stands for "Before Anyone Else."    * Reality: It is simply a shortened form of "babe" or "baby."
